title: OpenAPI 3.1 type:[X,null] on required properties generates non-Option field
description:
For OpenAPI 3.1 schemas where a property is BOTH listed in 'required' AND declared nullable via the 3.1 type-array form (type: ["string","null"]), the generator emits a non-Option field. Deserialization then fails against real responses that send null.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE RUNPOD v2 API. Two operations fail outright today:
- GET /v2/catalog/gpus  -> GpuType.pool is null in production; spec says type: ["string","null"], required. Generated: 'pub pool: String'.
- GET /v2/pods          -> Pod.template is null in production. Generated: 'pub template: String'.

Confirmed affected fields in https://api.runpod.io/v2/openapi.json (4, walking allOf branches):
  GpuType.pool, Pod.dataCenterId, Pod.template, Pod.startedAt

Pod.startedAt is the worst latent case: any pod that has not started returns null, which takes out the entire listPods call for that account.

Note Pod composes via allOf, so the required list and properties live in an allOf branch — a fix must traverse composition, not just top-level component properties.

Root cause reported by live-testing agent (unverified by me): nullability is computed as is_nullable() || is_nullable_pattern() in src/analysis.rs (~1936-1937, ~2506-2514), covering only 3.0 'nullable: true' and the anyOf-with-null shape. Schema::type_array_contains_null() (src/openapi.rs ~649-656) is called from only one site (analysis.rs ~1555). generator.rs (~2497-2517) then yields a plain String.

Closed issue openapi-generator-bgo fixed only the anyOf case; this type-array case is uncovered.

Severity: 3.1 is the modern dialect and this silently produces a client that cannot read production responses. This is first-run breakage of the worst kind — it compiles, then fails at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A required property declared type: ["string","null"] generates Option<String>, including when declared inside an allOf branch. Regression test covers both the direct component-schema case and the allOf-composed case. Generating the RunPod v2 spec yields Option for GpuType.pool, Pod.template, Pod.startedAt, and Pod.dataCenterId.
close_reason: Fixed in fad3ed3; verified against the live RunPod v2 API (list_gpu_types and list_pods now deserialize, with real nulls present in the responses). 362 tests pass.

title: full-spec-compile CI job is killed (SIGTERM 143) partway through the corpus
description:
The full-spec-compile job dies with exit code 143 (SIGTERM) roughly 25 minutes in, well under its configured timeout-minutes: 240. This is NOT a timeout.

Evidence it is pre-existing and environmental, not a code regression:
- 2026-07-20 scheduled run on main: full-spec-compile failed after 23 min; every other job passed.
- 2026-07-27 workflow_dispatch on a fix branch: failed after 29 min; every other job passed.
- The same scripts/spec-compile.sh passes locally on all 54 specs (54 passed, 0 gen-failed, 0 check-failed), run twice.

Failure point: the log shows an 11-minute silence after 'meta-llama PASS' and then SIGTERM. The next spec alphabetically is microsoft-graph, by far the largest in the corpus.

Likely cause (inference, not yet proven): runner resource exhaustion, most likely disk. The script routes all 54 isolated scratch crates through one shared SPEC_COMPILE_TARGET_DIR; locally that directory reaches 41 GB, while ubuntu-latest provides roughly 14 GB free. No explicit ENOSPC appears in the log, which is consistent with the runner terminating the process rather than cargo reporting it.

Impact: the README states a scheduled CI tier compile-checks all 54 OpenAPI specs. That tier has not been passing, so the claim is currently untrue and the corpus is effectively only verified locally.

Suggested approach:
1. Instrument first — log 'df -h' and memory before and after each spec's cargo check to confirm which resource is exhausted before changing anything.
2. If disk: free space on the runner (the standard ubuntu cleanup of preinstalled toolchains reclaims ~30 GB), and/or 'cargo clean' per spec, and/or shard the corpus across a job matrix.
3. If memory: reduce codegen parallelism for the largest specs.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled or dispatched full-spec-compile run completes and reports the summary line rather than being killed, and the resource hypothesis is confirmed by instrumentation rather than assumed.
close_reason: Root cause was memory, not disk or timeout: microsoft-graph generates 2.4M lines (16,153 operations) and peaks at ~14.3 GB RSS in a single rustc process, against 16 GB on ubuntu-latest. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 moved the peak 0.1%, ruling out parallelism/sharding fixes. Fixed in PR #42 by adding GENERATE_ONLY_SPECS to scripts/spec-compile.sh: microsoft-graph is still generated, only its cargo check is skipped, and it is reported in its own bucket so a green run cannot be mistaken for full verification. SPEC_COMPILE_FORCE_CHECK=1 checks it where there is headroom. Verified: full-spec-compile passed in CI (run 30235070971) for the first time — 53 passed, 0 failed, 1 generate-only, 1 skipped.

title: Client generator ignores SSE detection: streaming ops return () and hang forever
description:
Operations whose response is text/event-stream generate a client method returning Result<(), ApiOpError<..>>. The generated body calls response.text().await on an open SSE stream and discards the result. Since the stream never ends, the call never returns.

VERIFIED: GET /v2/pods/{id}/logs on RunPod v2 generates:
  pub async fn get_pod_logs(..) -> Result<(), ApiOpError<GetPodLogsApiError>>
The live-testing agent measured the call hung past 30s and past 600s. The generated HttpClient sets no timeout, so it deadlocks the caller's task rather than erroring. Raw SSE against the same endpoint works and returns well-formed frames.

The detection already exists and is correct: supports_streaming is computed in src/analysis.rs (~4562-4577) and the SERVER generator honors it (src/server/codegen.rs ~2263-2290). The CLIENT generator never reads it — reported as zero occurrences in client_generator.rs.

Two defects in one: (1) the streaming contract is dropped, (2) a discarded body plus no default timeout turns it into a hang instead of a visible failure.

Minimum fix: have client_generator consult supports_streaming and emit a streaming return type instead of (). Independently worth doing: give the generated client a default request timeout so a mis-generated call fails loudly rather than hanging.
acceptance_criteria: An operation declaring a text/event-stream response generates a client method returning a stream type rather than (), and does not call response.text() on it. Covered by a test over a spec with an SSE endpoint.
close_reason: Fixed in fad3ed3; verified against the live RunPod v2 API (list_gpu_types and list_pods now deserialize, with real nulls present in the responses). 362 tests pass.

title: Generated multipart clients miss reqwest multipart feature in REQUIRED_DEPS
description:
For specs with multipart/form-data operations, the generator emits client code calling reqwest::multipart::Form and RequestBuilder::multipart(), and correctly adds features=["multipart"] to reqwest-middleware in REQUIRED_DEPS.toml — but NOT to reqwest itself, which is pinned with default-features=false. The generated crate therefore fails to compile with E0433 (cannot find multipart in reqwest) and E0599 (no method named multipart on reqwest_middleware::RequestBuilder when its feature is also absent).

Reproducer: generate a client from https://api.studio.nebius.com/openapi.json (Nebius AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible, has POST /v1/files with multipart/form-data), then cargo check. Fails at client.rs with the two errors above.

Impact: hits any spec with a file-upload endpoint, including OpenAI's own spec. This is first-run breakage — the user runs the tool, the output does not compile, and they leave.

Fix: when any operation uses multipart/form-data, add "multipart" to the reqwest feature list in the emitted REQUIRED_DEPS.toml fragment (alongside the existing reqwest-middleware feature).
acceptance_criteria: Generating from a spec with a multipart/form-data operation produces a REQUIRED_DEPS.toml whose reqwest entry includes the multipart feature, and the resulting crate compiles clean. Covered by a corpus compile-check.
close_reason: Fixed in fad3ed3; verified against the live RunPod v2 API (list_gpu_types and list_pods now deserialize, with real nulls present in the responses). 362 tests pass.

title: Complete adoption and accessibility hardening program
description:
Complete the adoption and accessibility hardening program for gpu-cli/openapi-to-rust.

  This is an implementation goal, not merely an audit or plan. Work persistently until every in-scope deliverable is implemented, documented, tested, committed, and pushed. Follow AGENTS.md
  exactly. Run `bd prime` first, use Beads for all tracking, reconcile existing issues before creating duplicates, and push both Beads and Git state at completion.

  Do not publish a crates.io release without explicit approval. Prebuilt binaries, Homebrew, Scoop, and cargo-dist are out of scope for this goal; `cargo install` remains the primary
  installation path.

  1. Repair the configuration contract

  - Establish one canonical, documented type-mapping configuration shape, preferably `[generator.types]`.
  - Ensure the parser, Rust documentation, README, examples, generated comments, and tests all use the same shape and field names.
  - Preserve the currently parsed top-level `[types]` form as a temporary compatibility alias if feasible; reject configurations that specify both forms.
  - Remove or migrate the nonexistent/ignored `[generator.types.strategies]` form.
  - Reject unknown configuration fields instead of silently ignoring them, including nested sections.
  - Resolve paths relative to the configuration file rather than the caller’s working directory.
  - Add tests that parse every canonical example configuration and assert that the settings materially change generated output.
  - Provide clear migration errors or guidance for obsolete configuration forms.

  2. Fix `cargo install` packaging and dependency bloat

  - Configure Cargo so `cargo install openapi-to-rust --locked` installs only the `openapi-to-rust` executable.
  - Disable automatic binary discovery and move or feature-gate `catalog-gen` and `file-beads` as development tools.
  - Add functional `--version` support.
  - Align the generator’s direct reqwest dependency with reqwest 0.12 and eliminate the duplicated reqwest/Hyper 0.11 stack.
  - Remove generator dependencies that are referenced only inside emitted token streams.
  - Ensure `insta` and other test-only dependencies are not part of the default installed product; feature-gate public test helpers if they must remain available.
  - Remove or reduce unnecessary Tokio, reqwest, and other dependency features.
  - Investigate and resolve current future-incompatibility warnings where practical.
  - Add a CI installation smoke test that installs into a temporary root, asserts that only `openapi-to-rust` was installed, runs `--version`, and performs a minimal generation.
  - Verify with `cargo tree` that the default build no longer contains duplicate reqwest major versions.

  3. Make generated output compile without dependency guesswork

  - Replace the typed-scalar-only dependency reporting with a feature-aware generation-requirements collector.
  - Emit a complete, deterministic dependency manifest for every generated mode:
    - types;
    - async client;
    - retry and tracing;
    - SSE;
    - Axum server;
    - typed scalar features.
  - Include all required crate features and compatible versions.
  - Continue emitting a copyable Cargo manifest fragment and optionally print a corresponding `cargo add` command.
  - Do not silently modify a consuming project’s Cargo.toml by default.
  - Refactor the real-spec compile harness to consume the generated dependency manifest instead of a hardcoded dependency superset.
  - Add scratch-crate integration tests proving that types-only, client, SSE, server, and combined output compile using only the emitted dependency information.

  4. Correct README, CI claims, releases, and stale trackers

  - Remove the outdated `0.5` installation guidance and use a version-resilient CLI installation command.
  - Accurately distinguish:
    - specs parsed/generated on every PR;
    - specs cargo-checked on every PR;
    - the full local or scheduled compatibility corpus.
  - Do not claim that 54 specs are guarded by CI unless CI actually runs and gates that corpus.
  - Run generation/parsing across the whole bundled corpus on pull requests if reasonably fast.
  - Keep the production OpenAI and Anthropic compile checks on pull requests.
  - Measure the optimized full compile sweep on a clean runner and add a scheduled and/or release-gating workflow if its cost is reasonable.
  - Move detailed historical release notes from the README into CHANGELOG.md while keeping concise migration information.
  - Reconcile stale Beads against the current implementation. Verify acceptance criteria before closing anything.
  - In particular, audit the unsigned integer, format alias, typed additionalProperties, discriminator, and server-codegen Beads that appear stale relative to shipped code.
  - Close GitHub Issue #1 with a helpful comment linking the released Axum implementation and examples.
  - Update Issue #6 with implementation progress; close it only once its fix is genuinely available.
  - Resolve PR #21 deliberately: rebase and complete it if still wanted, or close it with a clear superseded/deferred explanation. Do not merge it merely for hygiene.
  - Add useful labels and milestones to the remaining public issues.

  5. Fix server-side query serialization and extraction symmetry

  - Make generated Axum servers correctly extract the same OpenAPI query shapes that generated clients serialize.
  - At minimum, fix form-exploded object parameters so handlers receive typed structs rather than impossible opaque strings.
  - Cover required and optional object parameters, arrays, explode=true, explode=false, and deepObject wherever the relevant wire representation is well-defined.
  - For unsupported or undefined combinations, fail or warn clearly at generation time rather than silently emitting incorrect code.
  - Reuse shared parameter-style analysis between client and server generation to prevent drift.
  - Add a generated client/generated server round-trip integration test that starts the Axum router, calls it with the generated client, and verifies the exact typed values received by the
  handler.

  6. Improve request construction and operation ergonomics

  Request models:
  - Automatically derive `Default` for generated object structs when every field can be defaulted safely, especially all-optional PATCH request bodies.
  - Add regression coverage using the Clerk-style `UpdateUserRequest` case from GitHub Issue #6.
  - For mixed required/optional request models, generate an ergonomic dependency-free builder:
    - required values supplied explicitly;
    - optional fields exposed as setters;
    - no complicated typestate system unless it materially improves the result.
  - Avoid adding new mandatory dependencies to generated projects.

  Operations:
  - Implement operation builders for methods with many optional parameters.
  - Preserve existing flat operation methods for compatibility; add an additive `*_builder` entry point unless a clearly documented migration is justified.
  - Keep required path/header parameters explicit and move optional query/header/body values to builder setters.
  - Provide `.send().await` using the existing generated request and response logic.
  - Make builder generation configurable with an enabled flag and threshold.
  - Add compile and snapshot tests for operations with many optional parameters and for body-field setters.
  - Ensure existing non-builder call sites continue to compile.

  7. Add a one-command trial path

  - Preserve advanced TOML-driven generation.
  - Also support an immediate path such as:
    `openapi-to-rust generate openapi.yaml --output-dir src/generated`
  - Support HTTPS spec URLs with sensible timeouts, response-size limits, and useful errors.
  - Add `openapi-to-rust init` to create a valid starter configuration from a local spec or URL.
  - Provide clear direct-mode defaults, with client generation enabled and an explicit types-only opt-out.
  - Add `--dry-run`, `--check`, `--quiet`, and machine-readable output where useful.
  - Ensure direct mode and config mode use the same parsing, validation, analysis, and generation pipeline rather than maintaining two divergent implementations.
  - Record source provenance in generated headers.
  - Add end-to-end CLI tests for local files, URLs through a local test server, initialization, dry-run, and stale-output checking.

  8. Improve discovery and community scaffolding

  - Rewrite the README’s opening so a visitor can understand the product and run it within 30 seconds.
  - Position it accurately as an OpenAPI 3.x Rust code generator for typed models, async clients, Axum servers, and SSE, with OpenAPI 3.2 explicitly marked experimental.
  - Include a small generated-code example, a concise compatibility statement, known limitations, and links to detailed configuration documentation.
  - Update Cargo and GitHub metadata to include Axum, OpenAPI 3.x, SDK generation, and Rust client/server terminology.
  - Add:
    - CONTRIBUTING.md;
    - CHANGELOG.md;
    - SECURITY.md;
    - Code of Conduct;
    - bug and feature issue forms;
    - pull request template;
    - support and compatibility guidance.
  - Create a contributor-friendly test workflow explaining fast checks versus the full spec corpus.
  - Add a few genuinely bounded `good first issue` candidates.
  - Improve crate-level documentation and examples for the stable public API; hide or feature-gate internal/testing APIs instead of documenting implementation internals solely to raise
  coverage.
  - Update GitHub repository topics and homepage/documentation links when authorized and supported.

  9. Add selective client generation

  - Add an opt-in `[client]` section supporting the same selector grammar as server generation:
    - operationId;
    - `METHOD /path`;
    - `tag:Name`.
  - Absence of `[client]` must preserve the current behavior of generating every client operation.
  - Add optional model pruning based on the transitive schema reachability of selected client operations.
  - When client and server generation are both active, retain the union of schemas reachable from both selections.
  - Reuse the existing selector parser and error/suggestion behavior.
  - Detect unknown, ambiguous, and renamed selectors with actionable errors.
  - Add tests for individual operations, methods/paths, tags, mixed client/server selections, model-pruning unions, and backward-compatible generate-all behavior.
  - Compile representative selective clients from large specs such as OpenAI, Stripe, Cloudflare, or Microsoft Graph.

  Global quality requirements

  - Preserve unrelated user changes and the existing untracked `.claude/worktrees/` directory.
  - Prefer additive generated APIs and documented migrations over unnecessary breaking changes.
  - Keep generated output deterministic.
  - Add regression tests before or alongside every bug fix.
  - Run, at minimum:
    - `cargo fmt --check`;
    - `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings`;
    - `cargo test --all-features`;
    - `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` with warnings denied;
    - cargo-install smoke testing;
    - OpenAI and Anthropic generated-code compilation;
    - the full real-spec generation/compile sweep where practical.
  - Update and close Beads only after their acceptance criteria are verified.
  - Create Beads for any genuinely deferred follow-up work.
  - Finish by committing all intended changes, pulling/rebasing safely, pushing Beads, pushing Git commits, and verifying that the branch is up to date with origin.
  - Provide a final handoff summarizing implementation decisions, compatibility changes, test results, tracker changes, and any deliberately deferred items.
notes: Published as draft PR https://github.com/gpu-cli/openapi-to-rust/pull/32 from codex/adoption-accessibility-hardening to main on 2026-07-15.

title: Support exploded query parameters (GH #27)
description: GH issue 27: query params with style=form, explode=true (OAS defaults) and object schemas currently map to Option<impl AsRef<str>> and are sent as one opaque string. Per OAS/RFC6570 form-explode, each object property must become its own query pair (?color=red). Fix: analyzer synthesizes/resolves a typed struct for object query params with form+explode semantics; client generator emits req.query(&struct) so reqwest/serde_urlencoded serializes properties as individual pairs.
notes: Implemented on branch issue-27-exploded-query-params, draft PR https://github.com/gpu-cli/openapi-to-rust/pull/28. Close when PR merges. Follow-ups: openapi-generator-anu (deepObject/explode=false/arrays), openapi-generator-0jz (server side).
close_reason: Released in v0.6.0 (PR #28)

title: Hybrid string-or-object discriminated unions deserialize-fail
description: When an anyOf/oneOf union contains a discriminator AND a non-object branch (e.g. string-enum like ToolChoiceOptions), the generator emits a tagged enum that cannot deserialize the string form. Real-world hit: OpenAI ToolChoiceParam returns 'auto' in Response.tool_choice, but generated type is #[serde(tag="type")] enum with no untagged String variant. Need to fall back to #[serde(untagged)] when the union mixes string/scalar branches with tagged-object branches, OR add a String fallback variant before the tagged variants.
notes: Live repro: `ToolChoiceParam` from openai.yaml line 52518. anyOf has 8 branches; the first (`ToolChoiceOptions`) is a string-enum ("none"|"auto"|"required"), the rest are objects with discriminator propertyName=type. Generator emits `#[serde(tag="type")] enum ToolChoiceParam { ToolChoiceOptions(ToolChoiceOptions), ... }` which cannot deserialize the string "auto" because serde tries to read a "type" field from a JSON string. Fix: when an anyOf/oneOf branch is a non-object schema (string/number/etc), the generator must emit `#[serde(untagged)]` with the scalar branch first OR add a String variant before the tagged variants. Hit on real OpenAI Responses API `Response.tool_choice` field.

title: [Server P2] Config schema + selector resolution

Schema:
  [server]
  framework = 'axum'        # required if section present; only 'axum' for v1
  operations = ["..."]    # list of selectors

Selector grammar (priority order):
  1. bare identifier            → operationId match
  2. 'METHOD /path'             → exact (method, path) match

title: [Server] Axum server codegen — umbrella
description:
Generate Axum server scaffolding for a user-selected subset of an OpenAPI spec's operations. Motivating case: hosting a replica of someone else's API (e.g. OpenAI POST /v1/chat/completions) without inheriting the entire spec surface.

Design doc: docs/planning/server-codegen.md

## Core principles
- Opt-in per operation (no default 'generate everything').
- Trait at the seam — user impl lives outside generated/.
- No scaffold file — all generated files are regenerable, all user files are hand-written.
- Spec drift surfaces loudly (renamed operationId → regeneration fails).
- No client-side validation in emitted code (existing project rule).

## Selection model
TOML [server].operations accepts three selector forms: operationId (recommended), 'METHOD PATH', or 'tag:Name'.

## Phases (separate issues)
1. server list CLI
2. config schema + selector resolution
3. server add / server remove CLI
4. trait + response-enum emitter
5. router factory + extractors + model pruning
6. snapshot tests against specs/openai.yaml (canonical: createChatCompletion)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] User can pick operations from openai.yaml via TOML or 'server add'.
- [ ] Generator emits trait + Router factory + typed response enums for picked ops only.
- [ ] User writes impl Trait for State in their own file; regeneration never touches it.
- [ ] models.rs pruned to types transitively reachable from picked ops.
- [ ] Snapshot test passes for createChatCompletion (non-streaming + SSE).

title: [Q4] Tagged discriminator enums (drop untagged when discriminator+mapping is present)
description:
When a schema has discriminator: { propertyName: 'type', mapping: { ... } }, we know exactly which type to deserialize at runtime by reading one field. Yet today we still emit #[serde(untagged)] on the union enum, which makes serde try every variant in order on every deserialization (slow) and emits the variant payload's JSON inline instead of a tagged shape on serialization (loses the discriminator on round-trip). Anthropic's content blocks (text/image/tool_use/tool_result) and OpenAI's response items are exactly this pattern. Tagged is much better. Approach: in generate_discriminated_enum, when the spec provides discriminator with mapping, emit #[serde(tag = '<discriminator.property_name>')] and rename each variant to the mapping value. For unions WITHOUT a discriminator, untagged remains.

## Context

title: [Q2] Format-typed scalars (date-time, uuid, byte, binary, ipv4, ipv6, uri)
description:

| date | chrono | chrono::NaiveDate | = "string" or "time" |
| time | chrono | chrono::NaiveTime | = "string" or "time" |
| duration | chrono | chrono::Duration | = "string" or "iso8601" |
| uuid | uuid | uuid::Uuid | = "string" |

## Context

- [ ] All 49 specs also still compile under --types-conservative.
close_reason: Q2 typed-scalar formats land with flipped defaults (chrono/uuid/url/bytes/std::net::Ip*Addr/base64+codec). TypeMappingConfig switched from Option<String> placeholders to enum-typed strategies (DateStrategy/UuidStrategy/ByteStrategy/...) with opt-out per format. Wired through SchemaType::Primitive's new serde_with field, surfaced via #[serde(with = ...)] in generator. base64_serde helper module (with Option submodule for nullable byte fields) emitted only when format:byte is actually used. type_lacks_default extended for chrono/url/time types. --types-conservative CLI flag collapses everything back to String for bisecting. spec-compile gate: all 54 specs pass with default typed-on config; 1 skipped (gitea, baseline). title: [Q1] Method-name canonicalization
description:

title: Server codegen: form-exploded object query params arrive as String
description: Follow-up to GH #27 (openapi-generator-cv4). title: [Server] Aggressive model pruning via analyzer-tracked synthetic ownership
description:
The current [server].prune_models implementation walks transitive $refs from picked ops, then keeps every schema not referenced by any $ref anywhere as a 'synthetic'. For OpenAI's spec this yields ~13% reduction because many real spec schemas are reached only via operations or multipart bodies, making 'never $ref'd' a poor synthetic signal.

To get >50% reduction safely, the analyzer needs to track which synthetic enums/structs belong to which parent schema. Concretely: when analysis registers WebSearchApproximateLocationType as a synthetic of WebSearchApproximateLocation's inline 'type: enum' field, it should record the parent→synthetic edge in DependencyGraph or in AnalyzedSchema (new field 'synthesised_from: Option<String>').

With that edge tracked, the prune walk becomes: walk transitive $refs from picked ops, then for every kept name, also keep all schemas whose synthesised_from points at it. That's both more aggressive and more correct than the current heuristic.

Related: the analyzer's existing AnalyzedSchema.dependencies field is also incomplete (Response.deps lists ResponseError but ResponseError.deps is empty even though it has a field of type ResponseErrorCode). Same root cause — analyzer registers synthetic siblings but doesn't track ownership.
notes:
Discovered while implementing prune_models in commit (current). Conservative impl ships; aggressive impl requires analyzer changes.
2026-07-15 audit during selective-client work: pruning now walks analyzed SchemaType ownership/reference edges and removes the old keep-every-unreferenced-schema heuristic, improving safety and precision. However the selective createResponse fixture pruned 127 of 344 analyzed schemas (36.9%), below this issue greater-than-50-percent target. Leave open until its specific acceptance metric is demonstrated on the intended full OpenAI server selection/corpus.

title: [Server] Anthropic spec missing text/event-stream content type on messages_post
description:
Anthropic's published OpenAPI spec (specs/anthropic.yaml) declares POST /v1/messages 200 response with content-type application/json only. The real API streams when stream:true is set on the request body, but the spec never declares text/event-stream as a valid response content type.

Consequence: 'server list' does not mark messages_post as [SSE], and downstream server codegen will not emit an SSE response variant for it. Both are technically correct given the spec text.

Mitigation options:
1. Use the existing schema-extensions mechanism to overlay a text/event-stream response on /v1/messages.
2. Add a config knob ('force_stream_for_operations') that promotes nominated ops to streaming regardless of declared response content.
3. Detect that the request body has a 'stream:bool' field and auto-promote (heuristic — risky).

Option 1 is the path that fits the existing project model. Add an example extension file documenting how to do this, and reference it from the server codegen docs once P6 lands.
notes:
Approach: make server list/add analyze the full generator config including schema_extensions; isolate the Anthropic example crate from the root workspace; make server example tests use Cargo's current binary path; update example docs; add focused regression coverage. Audit server implementation and PR official-client CI for adjacent high-confidence defects before closing.
Release target: 0.10.0 because corrected response status/SSE variants and wildcard/default payloads change regenerated public server APIs under the documented pre-1.0 policy.
close_reason: Reopened review findings and adjacent server audit issues are fixed: overlay-aware CLI, YAML overlays, reliable examples, official OpenAI/Anthropic SDK PR gates, faithful response semantics, and tag-collision diagnostics. All scoped and full all-features gates pass.

title: Propagate target schema nullability through $ref properties
description: When a $ref points to a schema that is itself anyOf[Object, null] (e.g. OpenAI ResponseError), the property using that $ref should be wrapped in Option<>. Currently we strip the null branch when analyzing the target schema and emit a struct, then properties referencing that struct don't pick up nullability. Real hit: OpenAI Response.error — we currently require nullable_overrides to handle it. Fix would record nullability on AnalyzedSchema and OR it in at the property level when the prop_type is a Reference. Lower priority since the override workaround is documented.

title: [Q5] Display for ApiOpError that surfaces the typed body
description:
Today format!('{e}', e: ApiOpError<E>) on an Api variant prints 'API error 404: {full body}'. For a Stripe error that includes a huge param_documentation blob, the message becomes a wall of JSON. Users complain they can't tell at a glance what the typed variant captured. Approach: in ApiError::Display, truncate body to ~500 chars with a '… (truncated)' marker; if typed.is_some(), prepend '(typed: <variant_name>)' (E: fmt::Debug bound already exists); if parse_error.is_some() and typed.is_none(), append '(parse error: …)'. Full body still accessible via .body field.

## Context
Files: src/http_error.rs. Evidence: src/http_error.rs:234 ApiError Display prints body verbatim — for huge JSON bodies this is unreadable; typed.is_some() info is hidden. See umbrella gpu-cli/openapi-to-rust#14.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ApiError Display truncates body at 500 chars (configurable via const).
- [ ] Typed variant name appears when typed.is_some().
- [ ] Parse error reason appears when typed parsing failed.
- [ ] Full body still accessible via .body — no info loss.
- [ ] Unit test in src/http_error.rs covers all three branches.
